info.name: bus_track API
info.description:
# bus_track API

A personal ferry-commute tracker. You record the legs of your ferry commute; the API
counts them into half days and full days.

**Base URL:** `{{base_url}}` — `http://localhost:8000` by default. Every endpoint is
prefixed with `/api` (Laravel's default API prefix).

---

## Getting started

1. Import this collection **and** `bus_track.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select **bus_track (local)** in the environment picker (top right). Nothing works
   without it — `{{base_url}}` and `{{token}}` live there.
3. Start the API:

   ```sh
   php artisan migrate --seed
   php artisan serve
   ```

4. Run **Auth → Register**, or **Auth → Login** with the seeded account
   (`test@example.com` / `password`).

   The token from the response is written into `{{token}}` by a test script on those two
   requests. Every other request inherits it through the collection's Bearer auth, so
   there is no token to copy and paste anywhere.

5. Run the rest in any order. **Ferry Trips → Record a day** also saves the created
   leg's id into `{{trip_id}}`, which makes **Delete a leg** runnable immediately.

---

## Authentication

Laravel Sanctum **personal access tokens**, sent as a header:

```
Authorization: Bearer 1|nQ8vK2mZ...
```

- Tokens are issued **only** by `POST /api/register` and `POST /api/login`.
- Tokens **never expire** (`config/sanctum.php` → `'expiration' => null`) and there is no
  refresh endpoint. Store one and reuse it.
- Every login mints a **new** token and leaves older ones valid.
- `POST /api/logout` revokes **only the token used for that request** — your other
  devices stay signed in. There is no "sign out everywhere".
- This is a pure token API. Cookie/SPA (stateful) mode is **not** enabled, so you never
  call `GET /sanctum/csrf-cookie` and never deal with CSRF or XSRF headers.

No token, a malformed token, or a revoked token on a protected route gives **401**
`{"message": "Unauthenticated."}`.

---

## How days are counted

A commute day has at most **two legs**: `morning` and `evening`. Each leg carries a
status, and only `taken` is worth anything:

| `status` | counts as | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `taken` | **0.5** day | you were on the ferry |
| `missed` | 0 | you did not make it |
| `cancelled` | 0 | the ferry did not run |

So a `day_count` is only ever `0`, `0.5`, or `1`. Both legs taken is a full day; one
leg is a half day. `missed` and `cancelled` are kept for history but add nothing to the
totals.

**These are floats, but PHP drops the trailing `.0`.** A full day arrives as `1`, not
`1.0`, and an empty month as `0`. Halves keep their decimal: `0.5`, `1.5`. In a typed
client, decode `day_count` and `total_days` as a float/double — decoding them as an
integer will work right up until someone takes a single leg.

Legs are unique **per user, per date, per leg** — there is a database constraint on
`(user_id, trip_date, leg)`. That constraint is why `POST /api/ferry-trips/day` upserts
instead of piling up duplicates.

---

## Conventions

- **Always send `Accept: application/json`.** Every request in this collection does.
- POST bodies are raw JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`.
- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Times are 24-hour `HH:MM` on the way in.
- The optional `month` query parameter is **strictly** `YYYY-MM`, e.g. `2026-09`.
  `2026-9`, `September` and `2026-09-01` are all rejected with 422. Omit it to get the
  current month.
- Everything is scoped to the authenticated user. You can never read or delete another
  user's trips.
- **No pagination anywhere** — a month holds at most ~62 legs, so reads return the whole
  month.
- Responses are plain JSON objects. There is no `data` wrapper and no envelope.

---

## Errors

Validation failures use Laravel's standard 422 envelope:

```json
{
  "message": "The trip date field must match the format Y-m-d.",
  "errors": {
    "trip_date": ["The trip date field must match the format Y-m-d."]
  }
}
```

Fields inside arrays are reported with dotted paths — `legs.0.status`, `legs.1.leg`.

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 201 | Created — **also returned when `POST /day` updates an existing leg** |
| 204 | Success with an empty body (logout, delete) |
| 401 | Missing, malformed, or revoked token |
| 404 | Trip does not exist **or** belongs to someone else |
| 422 | Validation failed — **including wrong login credentials** |
| 429 | More than 5 register/login attempts in a minute from one IP |

### Three things that surprise people

1. **A failed login is 422, not 401.** The error hangs off the `email` field:
   `errors.email[0] = "The provided credentials are incorrect."` — identically for a
   wrong password and for an unknown address. In this API, 401 only ever means "no valid
   token on a protected route".
2. **`/api/register` and `/api/login` are throttled to 5 requests per minute per IP.**
   Re-running Login while poking around returns 429 `{"message": "Too Many Attempts."}`
   with a `Retry-After` header. The ferry-trip routes are not throttled.
3. **`POST /api/ferry-trips/day` overwrites.** See that request's own documentation
   before calling it twice for the same date — fields you omit are cleared.

---

## Endpoints at a glance

| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/register` | — | Create an account, get a token |
| POST | `/api/login` | — | Get a token |
| GET | `/api/me` | Bearer | The current user |
| POST | `/api/logout` | Bearer | Revoke the current token |
| GET | `/api/ferry-trips` | Bearer | One month of legs, grouped by day |
| GET | `/api/ferry-trips/summary` | Bearer | Month totals (full / half / total days) |
| POST | `/api/ferry-trips/day` | Bearer | Record or correct one day's legs |
| DELETE | `/api/ferry-trips/{id}` | Bearer | Delete a single leg |
| GET | `/up` | — | Framework health check (not under `/api`) |

request.description:
Laravel's built-in health check. Use it to confirm `{{base_url}}` points at a running
server before you start debugging authentication.

`GET /up` · no auth · **not** under `/api`

Registered by `health: '/up'` in `bootstrap/app.php`. Returns **200** with a small HTML
page when the application boots; anything else (500, or a connection error) means the app
itself is broken rather than your request.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Getting and dropping a token.

**Register** and **Login** are the only public endpoints in the API and the only source
of tokens. Both are throttled to **5 requests per minute per IP** — a 429 while testing
just means you need to wait a minute.

Both write the returned token into `{{token}}` (and the user's id into `{{user_id}}`) via
a test script, so there is nothing to copy by hand. Everything in **Ferry Trips** then
picks it up from the collection's Bearer auth.

**Get current user** is the cheap way to check whether a stored token is still valid —
useful on app boot. **Logout** revokes the current token only.

// Written to both scopes: the environment wins if one is selected, the collection
// variable keeps things working if none is.

request.description:
Create an account and receive an API token in one call.

`POST /api/register` · no auth · **throttled to 5 requests/minute per IP**

### Body

| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | max 255 characters |
| `email` | string | yes | valid email, max 255, **must not already be registered** |
| `password` | string | yes | min 8 characters, must match `password_confirmation` |
| `password_confirmation` | string | yes | must equal `password` |

### 201 Created

```json
{
  "user": {
    "name": "Esther",
    "email": "esther@test.com",
    "updated_at": "2026-09-28T15:56:03.000000Z",
    "created_at": "2026-09-28T15:56:03.000000Z",
    "id": 2
  },
  "token": "2|nQ8vK2mZ7pR4tL9wX3cY6bF1hJ5sD0gA8eU2iO7k"
}
```

- `token` is the plain-text token — **this is the only time you will ever see it**. The
  server stores a hash. The token is named `react-app` server-side and never expires.
- `password` is never returned, for any endpoint.
- The freshly created user has no `email_verified_at` key at all (nothing has set it);
  `GET /api/me` returns it as `null`.
- The test script on this request stores `token` and `user_id` for you.

### Failures

| Cause | Code | Error key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email already registered | 422 | `email` |
| `password` shorter than 8 characters | 422 | `password` |
| `password_confirmation` missing or different | 422 | `password` |
| Any required field missing | 422 | that field |
| 6th attempt inside one minute | 429 | — (`{"message": "Too Many Attempts."}`) |

The body here uses a literal address rather than `{{email}}` so it does not collide with
the seeded user. Change the email if you re-run it — a second call with the same address
is a 422.

response.name: 422 Email already taken
422 Password too short / unconfirmed

request.description:
Exchange email and password for a bearer token.

`POST /api/login` · no auth · **throttled to 5 requests/minute per IP**

The body reads `{{email}}` and `{{password}}` from the environment, which ship pointing at
the account created by `php artisan db:seed` (`test@example.com` / `password`).

### Body

| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | yes | valid email |
| `password` | string | yes | — |

### 200 OK

```json
{
  "user": {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "Test User",
    "email": "test@example.com",
    "email_verified_at": "2026-09-28T15:56:03.000000Z",
    "created_at": "2026-09-28T15:56:03.000000Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-09-28T15:56:03.000000Z"
  },
  "token": "3|Xy7bQ2nR8vT4mK9wL3cF6hJ1sD5gA0eU7iO2pZ4k"
}
```

Note the status: **200**, not 201. Every call mints a **new** token and leaves existing
ones valid, so logging in five times leaves five working tokens.

### Failures

| Cause | Code | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrong password | 422 | `errors.email[0]`: `"The provided credentials are incorrect."` |
| Unknown email address | 422 | byte-identical to the above — the API will not tell you whether an address is registered |
| Malformed email or missing field | 422 | `errors.email` / `errors.password` |
| 6th attempt inside one minute | 429 | `{"message": "Too Many Attempts."}` + `Retry-After` |

**Bad credentials are 422, not 401.** If you are writing a client, read
`errors.email[0]` for the message to show the user, and reserve your "session expired"
handling for a genuine 401.

response.name: 422 Wrong password or unknown email

request.description:
The current user. The cheap way to check whether a stored token is still good.

`GET /api/me` · Bearer token

No parameters, no body.

### 200 OK

The user object **is the whole body** — there is no `user` wrapper here, unlike register
and login. Watch for that when writing a client.

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "name": "Test User",
  "email": "test@example.com",
  "email_verified_at": "2026-09-28T15:56:03.000000Z",
  "created_at": "2026-09-28T15:56:03.000000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-09-28T15:56:03.000000Z"
}
```

`email_verified_at` is `null` for accounts created through `POST /api/register` — there
is no verification flow in this API. `password` and `remember_token` are hidden by the
model and never appear in any response.

### Failures

| Cause | Code | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No `Authorization` header | 401 | `{"message": "Unauthenticated."}` |
| Token revoked by an earlier logout | 401 | same |

Revoke the token this request authenticated with.

`POST /api/logout` · Bearer token

No body.

### 204 No Content

Empty response body. The row is deleted from `personal_access_tokens`, so the same token
returns 401 from here on.

Only **this** token is revoked — tokens issued to your other devices keep working. There
is no endpoint that revokes everything.

### Failures

| Cause | Code |
| --- | --- |
| No token, or an already-revoked token | 401 |

After running this, `{{token}}` in your environment is dead: run **Login** again before
using the Ferry Trips folder.

item.name: Ferry Trips
item.description:
The trip log. All four endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` (inherited
from the collection) and operate **only on the calling user's own trips**.

Read with **List month** for every leg grouped by date, or **Monthly summary** for just
the totals. Write with **Record a day** — it upserts, so it is both "create" and "fix a
mistake". **Delete a leg** removes a single row by id.

Both read endpoints take the same optional `month=YYYY-MM` parameter and fall back to
the current month.

query.description: Optional. Exactly YYYY-MM (e.g. 2026-09). Omit or disable this row for the current month. 2026-9 and September are 422s.

request.description:
One month of recorded legs, grouped into days.

`GET /api/ferry-trips` · Bearer token

### Query parameters

| Param | Type | Required | Rules | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `month` | string | no | exactly `YYYY-MM` | the current month |

### 200 OK

```json
{
  "month": "2026-09",
  "days": [
    {
      "date": "2026-09-27",
      "morning": {
        "id": 1,
        "trip_date": "2026-09-27",
        "leg": "morning",
        "trip_time": "07:45:00",
        "status": "taken",
        "note": null,
        "created_at": "2026-09-27T07:50:11.000000Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-09-27T07:50:11.000000Z",
        "count": 0.5
      },
      "evening": null,
      "day_count": 0.5
    }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `month` | string | the month that was read, echoed back as `YYYY-MM` |
| `days` | array | **sorted by date ascending**; only dates with at least one recorded leg appear |
| `days[].date` | string | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `days[].morning` | object \| **null** | the leg object, or `null` when that leg was never recorded |
| `days[].evening` | object \| **null** | same |
| `days[].day_count` | float | `0`, `0.5` or `1` for that date — decode as a float, see below |

Things to know before you build a UI on this:

- **Null-check both legs.** A day with only a morning entry has `"evening": null` — the
  key is present but empty.
- Days with nothing recorded are **absent** from the array, not present with nulls. Zip
  it against your own calendar rather than assuming one entry per day.
- A leg's `count` is `0.5` when `status` is `taken`, otherwise `0`. `day_count` is the sum
  for that date.
- `trip_time` may be `null`, and **its precision depends on the database driver**: MySQL
  returns the `TIME` column as `"07:45:00"`, while SQLite echoes back the `"07:45"` that
  was written. Match on `HH:MM` and ignore any trailing seconds.
- `user_id` is hidden on every leg, by design.
- No pagination and no envelope: the whole month is in `days`.
- Only your own trips are visible. Another user's legs on the same dates are not merged
  in and cannot be seen.
- Month boundaries are exact: with `month=2026-09` you get 09-01 to 09-30 and nothing
  from August or October.

### Failures

| Cause | Code | Error key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `month=2026-9`, `month=September`, `month=2026-09-01` | 422 | `month` |
| No token | 401 | — |

A month with no trips is a normal **200** with `"days": []`.

request.description:
Month totals — the numbers you would put on an expense claim.

`GET /api/ferry-trips/summary` · Bearer token

### Query parameters

| Param | Type | Required | Rules | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `month` | string | no | exactly `YYYY-MM` | the current month |

### 200 OK

Exactly four keys, always present:

```json
{
  "month": "2026-09",
  "total_days": 1.5,
  "full_days": 1,
  "half_days": 1
}
```

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `month` | string | the month that was summarised, `YYYY-MM` |
| `total_days` | float | every `taken` leg counted as 0.5 and summed |
| `full_days` | int | dates where **both** legs were taken (`day_count >= 1`) |
| `half_days` | int | dates where **exactly one** leg was taken (`0 < day_count < 1`) |

`full_days + half_days` is the number of days you travelled at all, and
`total_days == full_days + half_days / 2`. The example above is one full day plus one
half day.

Dates where every leg was `missed` or `cancelled` count towards **none** of the three
numbers — they are not half days.

A month with no trips, or one where nothing was taken, returns **200** with
`total_days: 0, full_days: 0, half_days: 0`. Never a 404.

`total_days` is a float, but whole values arrive with no decimal point — `2`, never
`2.0`, while a month ending on a half day gives `2.5`. Decode it as a float/double.

### Failures

| Cause | Code | Error key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Badly formatted `month` | 422 | `month` |
| No token | 401 | — |

response.name: 200 One full day, one half day

request.description:
Record — or correct — the legs of a single day. This is the only write endpoint in the
API.

`POST /api/ferry-trips/day` · Bearer token

### Body

| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trip_date` | string | yes | exactly `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `legs` | array | yes | 1 or 2 items |
| `legs[].leg` | string | yes | `morning` or `evening`; if you send two, they must differ |
| `legs[].status` | string | yes | `taken`, `missed`, or `cancelled` |
| `legs[].trip_time` | string \| null | no | exactly `HH:MM`, 24-hour — `07:45`, `18:10`. **Not** `07:45:00` |
| `legs[].note` | string \| null | no | max 255 characters |

### It upserts — read this before calling it twice

There is a unique index on `(user_id, trip_date, leg)` and the controller uses
`updateOrCreate`, so posting the same `trip_date` + `leg` again **overwrites that leg**
rather than adding a second row. Four consequences:

1. The response is **201 Created even when it updated** an existing leg. Never treat 201
   here as "a new record was inserted".
2. **Fields you leave out are written as `null`, not left alone.** Re-posting
   `{"leg": "morning", "status": "taken"}` for a leg that already had a `trip_time` and a
   `note` **clears both**. Always send the complete state of the leg you are writing.
3. You can post one leg now and the other later — they are independent rows, and the
   second call does not disturb the first.
4. Sending `user_id` in the body has no effect. It is not mass-assignable and is always
   taken from your token, so you cannot write into someone else's log.

All legs in one request are written inside a database transaction: either every leg lands
or none does.

### 201 Created

```json
{
  "date": "2026-09-28",
  "trips": [
    {
      "trip_date": "2026-09-28",
      "leg": "morning",
      "trip_time": "07:45",
      "status": "taken",
      "note": null,
      "updated_at": "2026-09-28T08:01:44.000000Z",
      "created_at": "2026-09-28T08:01:44.000000Z",
      "id": 5,
      "count": 0.5
    }
  ],
  "day_count": 1
}
```

- `trips` comes back in the same order as the `legs` you sent.
- `day_count` is the new total for that date: `0`, `0.5`, or `1` — a float, but whole
  values arrive without a decimal point (`1`, never `1.0`).
- ⚠️ `trip_time` **echoes back exactly what you sent** (`"07:45"`) because the model is
  not re-read from the database. `GET /api/ferry-trips` does re-read it, so on MySQL the
  very same row comes back as `"07:45:00"`. Never compare the two literally.
- The test script on this request saves `trips[0].id` into `{{trip_id}}`, which makes
  **Delete a leg** runnable straight away.

### Failures

| Cause | Code | Error key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trip_date` not `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g. `28-09-2026`) | 422 | `trip_date` |
| `legs` missing, empty, or more than 2 items | 422 | `legs` |
| The same `leg` value twice in one call | 422 | `legs.0.leg` **and** `legs.1.leg` |
| `status` not one of the three allowed values | 422 | `legs.0.status` |
| `trip_time` not `HH:MM` (e.g. `07:45:00`, `7:45 am`) | 422 | `legs.0.trip_time` |
| `note` longer than 255 characters | 422 | `legs.0.note` |
| No token | 401 | — |

### Other bodies worth keeping

A half day — morning only:

```json
{
  "trip_date": "2026-09-27",
  "legs": [
    { "leg": "morning", "trip_time": "07:45", "status": "taken" }
  ]
}
```

Missed the morning, evening ferry was cancelled — `day_count` comes back `0`, and
`trip_time` is optional so it is simply left out:

```json
{
  "trip_date": "2026-09-26",
  "legs": [
    { "leg": "morning", "status": "missed", "note": "Overslept" },
    { "leg": "evening", "status": "cancelled" }
  ]
}
```

Both of these are saved as response examples on this request.

response.name: 422 Invalid status
422 Same leg twice

request.description:
Delete one recorded leg. There is no bulk delete and no whole-day delete.

`DELETE /api/ferry-trips/{ferryTrip}` · Bearer token

### Path parameter

| Param | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ferryTrip` | integer | yes | the leg's `id` — **not** a date. `{{trip_id}}` is filled in for you by **Record a day**. |

Ids come from `days[].morning.id` / `days[].evening.id` in **List month**, or from
`trips[].id` in **Record a day**.

Because an id identifies a single leg, clearing a full day takes two calls. If you only
want the day to stop counting, post it again with `status: "missed"` or `"cancelled"`
instead of deleting — that keeps the history.

No body. No soft deletes: the row is gone.

### 204 No Content

Empty response body.

### Failures

| Cause | Code | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Id does not exist | 404 | empty or framework-generated message — see the note below |
| The leg belongs to **another user** | 404 | deliberately indistinguishable from "does not exist", so the API cannot be used to probe for other users' ids |
| No token | 401 | `{"message": "Unauthenticated."}` |

The body of a 404 is **not** part of the contract: `message` is empty for an ownership
failure, and carries Laravel's "No query results for model ..." text (plus a stack
trace when `APP_DEBUG=true`) for an unknown id. Branch on the status code, never on
the message.

Deleting the same id twice gives 204, then 404.
